promptLatex: A fair six-sided die is rolled twice. What is the expected value of the smaller of the two rolls?
hintLatex: Count how many of the $36$ ordered pairs give each value for the minimum.
The minimum is $k$ on $2(6-k) + 1$ pairs, so the counts for $k = 1$ through $6$ are $11, 9, 7, 5, 3, 1$.
solutionLatex:
The smaller of the two rolls takes the value $1$ on $11$ of the $36$ ordered pairs, $2$ on $9$, $3$ on $7$, $4$ on $5$, $5$ on $3$, and $6$ on $1$.

E[\min] = \frac{1 \cdot 11 + 2 \cdot 9 + 3 \cdot 7 + 4 \cdot 5 + 5 \cdot 3 + 6 \cdot 1}{36} = \frac{11 + 18 + 21 + 20 + 15 + 6}{36} = \frac{91}{36}.

The minimum leans towards small values, so it is well below the midpoint of the range.
